pr.title: coverage: Restrict `ExpressionUsed` simplification to `Code` mappings
pr.description:
In the future, branch and MC/DC mappings might have expressions that don't correspond to any single point in the control-flow graph. That makes it trickier to keep track of which expressions should expect an `ExpressionUsed` node.

We therefore sidestep that complexity by only performing `ExpressionUsed` simplification for expressions associated directly with ordinary `Code` mappings.

(This simplification step is inherited from the original coverage implementation, which only supported `Code` mappings anyway, so there's no particular reason to extend it to other kinds of mappings unless we specifically choose to.)

Relevant to:
- #124154
- #126677
- #124278

processing.reason: PR #127758 changes only coverage-instrumentation bookkeeping: which expressions are marked "not-yet-seen" in LLVM coverage map data, and which BCBs are eligible to receive injected `ExpressionUsed` marker statements. The wrong transformation generalized `ExpressionUsed` injection/elision from ordinary `Code` mappings to Branch/MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision terms; the fix filters both sides to `Code` mappings. An `ExpressionUsed` statement is a coverage marker and does not change any computed value, control flow, or return value of the instrumented Rust function. Consequently there is no source-grounded pair of runtime functions whose observable numeric/boolean/character results differ: any such pair would have to fabricate an unrelated return-value difference or misrepresent the metadata-only rewrite, which the task forbids. The analysis itself states this is "not a confirmed runtime miscompilation; no compiler was built or executed," so no concrete executable counterexample can be validated.

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage must scope its `ExpressionUsed` simplification (eliding an injected use when an expression has no ordinary Code mapping) to expressions directly used by `MappingKind::Code`. The historical implementation treated expression terms from Code, Branch, and MCDCBranch mappings uniformly when deciding which expression IDs should be seen during MIR traversal. The PR aligns MIR-side `ExpressionUsed` injection with LLVM codegen-side "expressions seen" bookkeeping by introducing `bcbs_with_ordinary_code_mappings()` and filtering injection through that set. Branch and MC/DC expression terms are excluded because they may not correspond to a single CFG point/BCB. This is a coverage-mapping consistency change, not a confirmed runtime miscompilation; no compiler was built or executed.
analysis.trigger: A function is compiled with coverage instrumentation (`InstrumentCoverage`) and contains branch or MC/DC coverage mappings, especially expressions attached to conditional control flow. The problematic behavior arises when expression terms from non-Code mappings are treated as if each expression belonged to exactly one BasicCoverageBlock.
analysis.originalLogic: LLVM coverage map construction marked every expression ID appearing in any mapping term as "expected to be seen": `for term in function_coverage_info.mappings.iter().flat_map(|m| m.kind.terms())` followed by `if let CovTerm::Expression(id) = term { expressions_seen.remove(id); }`. `MappingKind::terms()` returned terms from Code, Branch, MCDCBranch, and MCDCDecision mappings (two terms for Branch/MCDCBranch). On the MIR side, `inject_coverage_statements` injected `ExpressionUsed` statements for coverage-expression BCBs selected by `bcb_has_coverage_spans`/counter-mapping eligibility. Thus both sides treated all mapping kinds' expressions as corresponding to CFG points.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to generalize the original Code-only `ExpressionUsed` simplification to every mapping kind: mark an expression as not-yet-seen if it appears in any `MappingKind` term, and inject `ExpressionUsed` at any BCB with coverage/counter mappings. This assumes branch true/false terms and MC/DC terms correspond to a single point in the control-flow graph. For Branch/MC/DC mappings that assumption can fail, so expression-use bookkeeping can disagree with the injected nodes. The corrected transformation only removes Code-mapping expression IDs from `expressions_seen`, and only injects `ExpressionUsed` for BCBs returned by `bcbs_with_ordinary_code_mappings()`, which iterates only `self.code_mappings`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions instrumented for source-based coverage whose extracted mappings include ordinary Code mappings and/or Branch/MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mappings. Two test programs can differ only in whether an expression used by branch or MC/DC coverage terms is also the term of an ordinary Code mapping at a single BCB; the fixed behavior restricts `ExpressionUsed` eligibility to the latter.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and mapping extraction has produced coverage mappings for the function.
The function has branch coverage or MC/DC mappings whose expression terms are not guaranteed to correspond to a single BCB.
The LLVM coverage-map 'expressions seen' initialization and the InstrumentCoverage MIR injection must use the same notion of eligible mappings; the patch comments require keeping these in sync.
pitfalls: Do not treat every `CovTerm::Expression` in every `MappingKind` as having a unique CFG location: `MappingKind::Branch` and `MCDCBranch` carry true/false terms and `MCDCDecision` carries none.
Do not remove `MappingKind::terms()` and assume no other callers; the patch removes it only after replacing the all-kinds traversal with a Code-only traversal.
Do not extend this eligibility only in LLVM map generation or only in MIR injection; both sides must agree, as the patch requires keeping the `ExpressionUsed` injection in sync.
Do not assume this PR proves an observed wrong runtime result; the description frames it as avoiding future complexity, and no compiler execution/reproduction is available.
The `num_bcbs` field is carried in `ExtractedMappings` so BCB bitsets can be allocated without the whole `CoverageGraph`; destructuring sites must account for the new field.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused coverage tests that compile small Rust functions with `-C instrument-coverage` and branch/MC/DC coverage enabled, then inspect the resulting coverage mappings/MIR rather than relying on runtime counters. Include (a) a function with only ordinary Code mappings and expressions, (b) a function with branch or MC/DC condition expressions, and (c) a function where the same expression/BCB is also covered by a Code mapping. Verify in the coverage output that `ExpressionUsed`/expression bookkeeping is emitted only for ordinary Code-mapping eligibility and that LLVM map initialization and InstrumentCoverage injection agree. Keep the differing input programs otherwise identical so the only variable is mapping kind / Code eligibility. Report static inspection of test expectations and patch behavior; do not claim execution.
